sentences.text:
This Appeal is filed by the appellants/claimants, under Section 173 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988,
aggrieved by the order and decree dated 15.03.2013 passed in O.P. No.1770 of 2011 by the IX Additional Chief Judge, City Civil Court, Hyderabad (Fast Track Court) (for short, "the Tribunal"),
whereby the Tribunal awarded compensation of Rs.7,23,500/- with interest at 7% per annum in favour of the appellants/claimants, for the death of D. Suresh (hereinafter referred to as "the deceased") in a motor vehicle accident.

entities.text: IX Additional Chief Judge, City Civil Court, Hyderabad (Fast Track Court
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 2. The brief facts of the case are that on 22.04.2011 at about 8:00 PM, while the deceased was proceeding on foot near Guest House, Shankarpally, a Honda Shine motorcycle bearing No. AP 28 DG 1777, driven in a rash and negligent manner, dashed against him from behind, resulting in grievous injuries.
Though he was shifted to hospital, he succumbed to the injuries while being shifted to another hospital.

The appellants/claimants, being the wife, minor daughters and mother of the deceased, filed the aforesaid claim petition under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act before the Tribunal, claiming compensation of Rs.10,00,000/- on account of the death of the deceased.

The Tribunal, upon appreciation of evidence, held that the accident occurred due to the rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle and awarded a total compensation of Rs.7,23,500/- with interest at 7% per annum, fastening liability on both respondents.
Aggrieved thereby, the appellants/claimants filed the present appeal seeking enhancement of compensation.

3. Learned counsel for the appellants contended that the Tribunal awarded meagre amounts under conventional heads; that the overall compensation granted by the Tribunal is grossly inadequate;
and thus prayed for enhancement of compensation.

Learned counsel also contended that interest at 7.5% per annum should be awarded as per the decision of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of National Insurance Company Ltd. vs. Mannat Johal and others 1.

sentences.text: On the other hand, learned Standing Counsel appearing for respondent No.2-Insurance Company supported the award passed by 1 AIR 2019 SC 2079 the Tribunal and contended that the compensation granted is just and reasonable, and does not warrant any interference.

5. There is no dispute with regard to the occurrence of the accident and the finding of the Tribunal that the accident occurred due to the rash and negligent driving of the rider of the offending motorcycle.
The said finding has attained finality.

6. So far as quantum of compensation is concerned, the Tribunal, upon considering the evidence on record, fixed the monthly income of the deceased at Rs.4,500/- and, after deducting 1/4th towards personal expenses and applying multiplier '17', awarded Rs.6,88,500/- towards loss of dependency.

The Tribunal further awarded amounts towards transportation and medical expenses at Rs.10,000/- and Rs.10,000/- respectively, which appear to be just and reasonable and they are accordingly confirmed.
However, the Tribunal has awarded only meagre amounts under conventional heads i.e., Rs.15,000/- towards funeral expenses.

As per the principles laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in National Insurance Co. Ltd. v. Pranay Sethi 2, the appellants-claimants are also entitled to Rs.91,000/- (Rs.70,000/- + 10% enhancement for every three years) under the conventional heads.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Thus, the total compensation payable to the appellants/claimants is re

7. Coming to the rate of interest, as the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Mannat Johal's case (supra) and in several subsequent decisions held that the reasonable rate of interest to be awarded in motor accident claim cases shall be 7.5% per annum, this Court is of the opinion that the rate of interest awarded by the Tribunal in the instant case is on the lower side and the same requires modification.

8. In the result, the appeal is partly allowed enhancing the compensation awarded by the Tribunal from Rs.7,23,500/- to Rs.7,99,500/- with interest at 7.5% per annum from the date of petition till the date of realization.
The remaining terms and conditions of the Tribunal shall stand unaltered.
No order as to costs.
As a sequel, the miscellaneous petitions pending, if any, shall stand closed.
